L109.formula: pair(A)=T; pair(T)=A; pair(G)=C; pair(C)=G; lower strand left-to-right has 3-prime to 5-prime direction

parameters.upper_sequence: 6 bases, selected position cycles A,T,G,C; upper left=5-prime
parameters.base_pair: two nucleotides; whole fragment has12 nucleotides

assumptions: Sequence order carries information; colours do not
A=T/G=C totals apply to complete paired double strand, not necessarily an isolated strand
limits: Flattened schematic not to scale or a genome
No replication enzymes, chromatin or phenotype prediction
Clicking edits a teaching model, not biological material

protein_coding: translation joins amino acids; protein folds/functions

assumptions: DNA remains a source of information, not converted into protein material
RNA and protein quantities are different relative indicator scales
Functional RNA can also act in nucleus
Gene presence does not guarantee equal expression
limits: RNA processing, expression regulation and codon mechanics omitted
No one-gene-one-trait or fixed RNA/protein yield claim
Eukaryotic location model does not apply unchanged to prokaryotes

parameters.C: unreplicated haploid DNA amount, fixed throughout
parameters.all_counts: per cell at COMPLETED checkpoints, not transient anaphase

assumptions: Perfect segregation; no DNA loss; replicated total4C conserved across subsequent divisions
X represents one replicated chromosome with two joined sister chromatids
limits: Crossing over and many division structures omitted for counting clarity
Transient anaphase counting uses different boundaries
Meiotic products in plants do not always directly become gametes
Homologue colour indicates illustrative origin, not gene identity or selection for need

parameters.G: 0–6 contributing allele units across three independent two-allele loci
parameters.Y: fictional plant-height units, not cm or a real cultivar
parameters.frequency: expected counts across64 equally probable allele combinations, not a sampled population

assumptions: Each allele is equally frequent and independent in the combinations
Equal additive allele contributions plus explicit G*E interaction
Fixed expected group counts; changing environment changes trait values, not allele frequencies
No measurement noise or within-genotype environmental variation
limits: Seven discrete expected groups, not a real continuous sample
No empirical fit and no human ability/health/social prediction
Distribution shape alone cannot separate genetic/environmental mechanisms
Cannot estimate real heritability from this demonstration
